r2-building-01.observations: Roof shingles retain dense granular highlights and dark rounded relief, matching the rectangular roof on the reference sheet. Plaster retains fine irregular dots and original-sized timber outlines. Contrast and eave shading fit the references. One visible wooden door.

r2-building-02.observations: The steep roof preserves fine red shingle relief and the reference's bright stepped treatment on the left plane. Gable and both plaster stories retain small irregular grain, thin framing, and shaded upper edges. The upper openings are windows; one wooden door is visible downstairs.

r2-building-03.observations: Intersecting roof sections retain granular shingles, bright left-facing tile edges, and darker right-facing roofing. Plaster dots and timber thickness remain compatible with the originals. The foreground wing has one wooden entry; the exposed background below the rear wing does not show another enclosed-room entrance.

r2-building-04.observations: The wider roof maintains small highlighted shingles and a darker hip plane without coarse replacement marks. Both plaster stories preserve fine stippling, narrow timber braces, and reference-compatible contrast. Five windows and one ground-floor wooden door are visible.

r2-building-05.observations: Roof tiles preserve the original fine warm highlights and dark relief. Stone walls use small irregular pale stones, purple mortar, and granular variation consistent with the stone and church references. Eave shading and outlines remain compatible. One window and one wooden door are visible.

issues.reason: Large repeated angular tan marks and broad horizontal brown bands replace the reference's dense, individually shaded shingles. Rounded tile relief and fine texture density are missing.
Plaster infill is almost solid, without the original fine irregular grain. Heavy boxed framing and the coarse rectangular plinth create a substantially different rendering style.
Muted tan and olive outlines give framing, infill, and opening surrounds much weaker value separation than the reference's dark contours and crisp small highlights.
Broad flat roof shading and straight rim highlights provide little tile or plane relief. The wall beneath the overhang lacks the reference's pronounced shaded upper plaster band.

sample-11.observations: The roof has sparse manufactured-looking marks; walls have flat cream panels, thick rectangular surrounds, and a coarse block base. Contrast and surface lighting differ materially from the originals. One central wooden door and two windows are visible.

r2-building-06.observations: Dense orange shingles retain small rounded highlights and dark recesses. Cream plaster preserves fine speckling, with timber and wooden entry rendered at compatible pixel scale. Roof, chimney, and facade contrast fit the references.

r2-building-07.observations: The roof has granular tile relief, with brighter shingles on the left plane and darker orange-purple shingles on the right. Both gable and lower plaster retain fine dots. Timber thickness, warm palette, and shading match the established style.

r2-building-08.observations: Orange roof tiles preserve the original highlight size and plane shading. Both stone wall levels contain small mottled stones, irregular highlights, and dark joints rather than plain grid cells. The gable stonework and teal opening remain compatible with the original stone building.

r2-building-09.observations: Blue roofing preserves the reference church's bright raised rows and darker granular shingles across the lower roof and spire. Pink-gray masonry retains fine mottling and pale structural bands. Roof highlights, recessed windows, and wall contrast agree with the original church.

r2-building-10.observations: The roof and stone facade closely match the original stone anchor: rounded bright tiles on the left, dense darker shingles on the right, and finely mottled masonry around the entry and gable. Outlines, palette, and directional contrast are compatible.

r3-building-01.observations: Intersecting roofs retain dense, rounded shingle relief, fine highlights and darker opposing planes. Plaster stippling and timber outlines match the reference scale. One front wooden entry is visible; the right facade object is a pictorial sign.

r3-building-02.observations: Golden gables preserve granular tile relief and plane-dependent highlights; connecting orange roofing retains the reference texture density. Walls use fine plaster dots and compatible timber framing. One lower-left wooden door is visible. Ground between the wings is outdoor space; the other framed openings are windows.

issues.reason: A rectangular cream notch interrupts the canopy's tiled front lip. Shingle rows end abruptly around it without a framed roof opening or a continuous finished eave.

r3-building-03.observations: Main roofing and canopy retain fine orange-purple shingle texture, and the plaster retains reference-sized stippling. The canopy's central lower edge visibly breaks that otherwise coherent finish. The left wooden entry remains exposed; the counter does not conceal it.

r3-building-04.observations: Olive roofing preserves small rounded tile clusters, dense shadow pixels and directional highlights across the main and annex planes. Cream plaster grain and narrow timber outlines remain compatible. The changed roof color maintains readable contrast. One wooden entry is visible.

r3-building-05.observations: Blue tower shingles and orange gable tiles retain the original sheet's fine relief and left-lit highlights. Masonry has dense small mortar marks and stone grain rather than broad flat blocks. One wooden entry is visible in the lower right body; tower glazing and the circular gable window are not entries.

r3-building-06.observations: Orange roofs retain dense shingles with small highlights, dark tile relief, and shaded adjoining planes. Plaster retains fine mottled flecks and compatible timber line weight. One visible ground-floor door; the framed emblem is a sign.

r3-building-07.observations: Gabled roofs preserve granular orange shingles, bright left-facing courses, and darker right-facing tiles. Walls retain fine plaster speckling and original-sized framing. One wooden door is visible; the central gap is outdoor space and the upper framed object is a sign.

r3-building-08.observations: Orange and slate-blue roofs both retain small shingle highlights and dark granular relief. The blue gable distinguishes its bright and shaded planes. Plaster flecks and timber thickness remain compatible with the reference. The ground-floor door remains visible beside the signs.

r3-building-09.observations: The taupe roof cap retains dense highlighted and shadowed shingle marks with a dark underside. Tapered plaster walls preserve fine speckling, edge shading, and a granular stone foundation. Contrast is quieter than the orange reference but texture remains legible. One arched wooden entry is visible.

r3-building-10.observations: The tan main roof retains tightly packed tile relief and bright ridge highlights; the orange gable preserves the reference's shingle granularity. Plaster panels retain fine flecks and compatible timber outlines. One door is visible in the smaller wing; the lower-right framed object is a sign.

r6-building-01.observations: Brown roofing retains dense staggered shingles, small highlight rims, and recessed dark joints. The right roof area is darker. Cream plaster preserves fine speckles beneath narrow timber framing. Warm browns and teal glazing fit the reference contrast. One wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-02.observations: Slate-blue shingles have closely packed highlights and dark relief at compatible native pixel scale. Both facade levels retain fine plaster grain and narrow timber seams. Roof shading, cream walls, and warm wood accents remain compatible with the references. One ground-floor door is visible.

r6-building-03.observations: Ochre roofing shows dense staggered tile relief and small bright caps along the upper edge. Pink-gray masonry preserves irregular stone mottling and fine dark mortar comparable to the original stone buildings. Chimney and facade shading are coherent. One wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-04.observations: The curved olive roof retains small, densely packed shingle highlights and shadows, with darker rendering toward the right edge. Plaster speckles and thin timber framing match the reference grain scale. Earthy colors and directional shading remain compatible. One wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-05.observations: The blue conical roof has dense shingle relief with small highlights and a darker right side. Tower plaster carries fine scattered flecks and stepped side shading; the stone plinth retains granular masonry detail. Blue, cream, and brown values fit the reference style. One arched wooden entry is visible.

r6-building-06.observations: Taupe roofing retains dense staggered shingles, small raised highlights and dark tile recesses. Plaster preserves fine pixel speckling and reference-sized timber edges. Ridge, chimney and eave shading remain compatible with the originals.

r6-building-07.observations: Orange and olive roofs retain granular tile relief, bright left facets and darker right facets. Fine plaster dots, narrow timber framing and small window accents match the reference texture scale. Both roof sections use compatible lighting.

r6-building-08.observations: Slate roofing has dense shingle marks and clearly differentiated hip-plane shading; the orange wing retains rounded tile highlights and dark creases. Dotted plaster and thin timber edges preserve the original grain. Roof, chimney and facade shadows agree.

r6-building-09.observations: The bulbous tan roof carries dense granular shingles with curved, compressed rows around its crown and shoulders. Brighter left surfaces and darker right edges describe its volume. Plaster speckling and timber outlines retain reference-scale detail and contrast.

r6-building-10.observations: Both rounded roofs retain dense shingle relief with curved rows and darker right surfaces. Tower plaster preserves fine dots and cylindrical shading; house plaster and foundation stone retain granular detail. Outlines, warm material colors and lighting fit the references.

r7-building-01.observations: Dense orange shingles retain rounded highlights and dark overlaps comparable to the original stone building. Irregular stone courses and fine mortar pixels preserve its wall grain. Lighting and outline weight fit; one wooden entry is visible.

r7-building-02.observations: Olive roofing preserves small tile highlights, recessed seams, and darker receding roofing. Plaster retains fine scattered specks within appropriately sized timber framing. The recoloring remains compatible with the references; one wooden entry is visible.

r7-building-08.observations: Both tall roofs and the connecting roof retain dense warm shingles with rounded relief and consistent light direction. Gables and facade preserve fine plaster specks, narrow timber framing, and dark recesses. Arched glazing reads as windows; one ground-floor wooden entry is visible.

r7-building-09.observations: The large blue-gray roof retains dense small shingle highlights and dark overlap marks rather than enlarged texture cells. Speckled plaster and timber framing maintain the reference detail scale. Cool roof tones and eave shadows remain compatible; one ground-floor wooden entry is visible.

r8-building-01.observations: Warm shingles retain granular rounded highlights and shaded gaps. The plaster gable and timber facade retain fine original-scale speckling and restrained outlines. Upper arched openings read as windows; one wooden entry is visible below.

r8-building-02.observations: Ochre shingles retain dense staggered highlights and small dark tile separations, with coherent shading across the roof hips. Cream plaster retains fine scattered flecks; timber, arched windows, and outlines remain compatible with the original rendering.

r8-building-06.observations: Orange-red roofing preserves dense rounded tile relief and a brighter left roof plane. The triangular gable and stone walls retain small irregular masonry marks and fine mortar shading; teal glazing and warm window trim fit the reference palette.

r8-building-07.observations: Olive roofing maintains fine shingle density, individual highlights, and a darker right hip. Pink-gray masonry retains granular stone and mortar detail; facade bands and window outlines have compatible thickness and contrast.

r9-building-01.observations: Dense orange-red tile marks and the mottled stone gable closely follow the original stone building's rendering. The lower wall has small varied light stones separated by dark mauve mortar, with compatible grain scale and directional lighting.

r9-building-02.observations: Ochre-olive shingles retain fine staggered relief and distinct shading across the roof planes. Cream plaster preserves tiny scattered flecks; brown timber, teal windows, and restrained outlines remain consistent with the reference style.

r9-building-03.observations: Both orange roofs retain dense, small shingle highlights and shaded undersides. Plaster keeps fine dotted grain and narrow timber edges; palette and lighting remain compatible across both masses.

r9-building-04.observations: Slate lower roofing and the orange upper roof preserve fine shingle density and highlights following their planes. Plaster speckles and timber thickness match the references; cool roofing retains compatible contrast and illumination.

r9-building-05.observations: Slate shingles retain small overlapping relief, a brighter left slope, and darker right-facing detail. All three plaster stories preserve fine grain and original-sized timber outlines; the cool palette fits the established rendering.

r9-building-06.observations: Orange tower roofing and slate wing roofing retain granular shingles and consistent lighting from the left. The gable and walls preserve dense irregular masonry grain and compatible contrast. Narrow dark windows remain visually distinct from the single wooden door.

r9-building-07.observations: Both tower caps and the connecting orange roof retain dense shingle relief at the reference dot scale. Fine plaster speckles, narrow timber outlines, warm material ramps, and highlight direction remain consistent across the facade.

r9-building-08.observations: Dense blue-gray shingles retain small rounded highlight/shadow clusters and fine dark seams. The darker right roof plane supports the lighting. Plaster has fine tan speckling and reference-scale timber outlines; the slate colors remain compatible.

r9-building-09.observations: Both ochre house shingles and blue-gray tower shingles show dense, small relief marks. House plaster and tower plaster retain fine speckling; the masonry footing has granular joints. Darker right edges agree with the roof highlights.

r9-building-10.observations: Brown and ochre roofs retain tightly packed shingle highlights and dark relief at the original dot scale. The gable and timbered walls retain fine plaster flecks. Roof-plane shading, warm wood and teal glazing remain compatible with the anchors.

r9-building-11.observations: The ochre hip roof and blue-gray pointed roof use dense shingle clusters with small highlights and shaded seams. Both facade levels retain fine plaster speckles and narrow framing. Brighter left roof edges and darker right slopes give compatible lighting.

r9-building-12.observations: The orange roof preserves dense rounded tile relief, strong yellow highlights on the left plane and darker red seams on the right. Gable and wall plaster retain fine scattered grain with narrow brown framing. Contrast and lighting closely match the reference.

r9-building-13.observations: Khaki shingles retain small highlighted tile crowns, dense dark seams, and a darker right roof plane. Plaster retains fine scattered flecks and reference-sized timber outlines. The changed roof color preserves compatible contrast and lighting.

r9-building-14.observations: Blue-gray roofing has densely packed shingles with small bright edges and recessed dark seams; the right hip is darker. Cream plaster keeps the original fine stipple and narrow brown framing. Roof, windows, and facade maintain compatible shadow contrast.

r9-building-15.observations: Both orange roofs retain granular tile relief, bright tile ends, and fine dark separations with shading following their planes. The gable and facade have small plaster flecks and matching timber weight. Warm roofing, teal windows, and brown wood fit the references.

r9-building-16.observations: The slate hip and orange gable preserve small, closely packed shingle highlights and dark seams, with distinct roof-plane shading. Both sections share finely flecked plaster and reference-sized brown framing. The two roof palettes maintain compatible light and contrast.

r9-building-17.observations: Orange roofing retains fine tile seams, highlighted tile ends, and a darker right slope. The gray stone pediment and pink-gray masonry preserve irregular stone shapes and dense small mottling consistent with the stone and church anchors. Dark windows and warm wood retain compatible contrast.

r9-building-18.observations: Olive roofing retains dense, staggered tile relief, small highlights, and a darker right hip. Masonry has fine irregular flecks and narrow joints compatible with the original church stonework. One lower wooden entry is visible.

r9-building-19.observations: Terracotta and olive roofs preserve granular, staggered shingles with rounded highlight and shadow clusters. Plaster panels retain fine mottling within narrow timber framing. Roof facets receive compatible directional shading; the teal openings read as windows.

issues.reason: The visible sloped roofing uses long, smooth diagonal bands instead of dense staggered shingles with small rounded highlights and recesses.
Broad log strips have nearly uniform fills and isolated dark nicks. Chunky pale corner caps further depart from the reference's fine grain and thin edging.

r10-building-01.observations: The roof reads as striped boards; the gable and lower walls repeat broad horizontal log bands with sparse surface marks. Warm wood colors and brighter left roof shading are compatible, but texture density and relief materially differ.

issues.reason: The narrow roof slopes are smooth brown ribbons with continuous highlights, lacking the original's granular, rounded shingle relief.
The facade repeats flat horizontal strips with sparse notches and large pale end blocks, losing the reference's fine surface texture and outline scale.

r10-building-02.observations: Roof edges show continuous bands rather than individual textured shingles. Gable and wall logs contain broad flat fills between horizontal rails. The brown, teal, and green palette and general light direction are compatible.

issues.reason: Long diagonal roofing bands lack the reference's dense staggered tile clusters, rounded relief, and fine local grain.
Large areas of uniform horizontal log fill contain only occasional dark marks; thick pale corner blocks make the facade substantially coarser than the originals.

r10-building-03.observations: The roof has smooth diagonal stripes, while the exposed wall and gable use repetitive horizontal rails with sparse grain. Warm colors and left-to-right roof shading fit, but the surface rendering remains too broad and graphic.

issues.reason: Long diagonal highlight/shadow bands dominate the roof plane. They lack the reference's dense individual shingles, rounded relief and small staggered highlights.
Full-width log stripes, regularly spaced dark notches and chunky bright corner ends produce coarse repeated banding rather than the reference's fine, varied surface grain.

r10-building-04.observations: Roof slopes read as striped wood; walls repeat broad horizontal logs with sparse notch marks. Warm browns, teal panes and upper-left roof highlights are compatible. One lower door is visible.

issues.reason: Continuous diagonal roof stripes replace dense overlapping shingles. Small rounded tile relief and granular variation remain absent.
Broad repeated log courses and bright block-shaped corner ends overwhelm the sparse surface marks. The grain scale and repetition differ materially from the original rendering.

r10-building-05.observations: Window flowers add small color accents, but the roof remains broadly striped and the walls retain coarse log banding. Palette and lighting are coherent. One unobstructed lower door is visible.

issues.reason: Roof shading consists of long parallel bands with little individual shingle articulation. It does not reproduce the original's dense rounded tile texture.
Uniform horizontal log stripes, repeated notch marks and chunky pale corner blocks retain a coarse graphic surface instead of original-scale granular variation.

r10-building-06.observations: Green shutters and a teal lower door fit the color family. They do not change the striped roof or repetitive wall texture. Roof highlights and eave shadows are coherent; one lower entrance is visible.

issues.reason: Visible roof surfaces are narrow continuous diagonal bands around a horizontally striped gable. No dense individually shaded shingle field establishes the reference's roof grain.
Repeated full-width log courses and oversized bright corner ends create a coarse ladder-like texture. Sparse dark notches do not supply the original's fine surface density.

r10-building-07.observations: The smaller building still has striped roof edges and repetitive log walls. Warm colors and highlight direction are coherent. A square window sits above one lower door.
